payload.task_text:
You are working for a music label as a curator who needs to compile an official tracklist from a recent Afrobeat mix video that has been circulating online. The mix video has the identifier 7ZQzGq32kAY and was published by a music channel. Your job is to extract all distinct song titles and artists featured in the mix, organize them into a structured spreadsheet, write a curator notes document, publish the tracklist to the team wiki, and email the final results.

Start by retrieving the video metadata for 7ZQzGq32kAY to confirm the video title and channel information. Then fetch the full English-language transcript of the video. Carefully read through the transcript to identify individual songs mentioned. Look for patterns where song titles and artist names appear together, typically with a separator between the song title and the artist name. Extract every distinct song title and the associated artist name. Estimate each song's start time in seconds based on where it first appears in the transcript, and estimate its duration in seconds before the next song begins. The mix contains at least ten songs and likely more.

Create a spreadsheet file named Afrobeat_Tracklist.xlsx. Inside this file, create a sheet called Tracklist with the following columns in order: Track_Number (starting from 1 and incrementing for each song), Song_Title (the name of the song), Artist (the performing artist or featured artists), Start_Time_Sec (the estimated start time in seconds from the beginning of the mix), Duration_Sec (the estimated duration of that track in seconds), and Notes (a brief one-phrase description of the track style or significance). This sheet must contain at least ten data rows. Also create a second sheet in the same file called Artist_Summary with columns Artist, Song_Count (number of tracks by that artist), and Total_Duration_Sec (sum of all their track durations). This summary sheet must have at least four rows representing different artists.

Next, create a Word document named Curator_Notes.docx. Begin with a heading "Afrobeat Mix 2024 - Curator Notes". Add a summary section that states the total number of tracks identified and the number of unique artists found in the mix, along with an estimate of the total mix duration in seconds. Then add a section called Notable Tracks that highlights five standout songs from the tracklist with a brief sentence about each one explaining why it stands out. Finally add a section called Genre Analysis that describes the musical styles and regional variations of Afrobeat represented in the mix, covering at least two distinct style observations.

Publish the tracklist information to the team wiki by creating a new page titled "Afrobeat Mix 2024 Tracklist". Add the full tracklist as content blocks on this page, listing each track number, song title, and artist. Also add a summary of the Artist Summary data showing how many tracks each artist contributed.

Finally, compose and send an email to music@label.com with subject "Afrobeat Mix 2024 Tracklist Ready". The email body should mention that the analysis is complete, state the number of tracks identified, reference the attached spreadsheet file, and invite the recipient to review the curator notes document for further detail.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent freezes one explicit full-timeline contract into a canonical payload first, then dispatches exactly one wave of three parallel coder sub-agents (workbook, document, and wiki writers), and sends the final email itself at acceptance. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload and the three writer contracts below are the complete plan, used consistently by every output.

Dynamically resolve the workspace. Call get_video_info(url="7ZQzGq32kAY") once to confirm the video title and channel; then exhaust both get_transcript(url="7ZQzGq32kAY", lang="en", next_cursor=...) and get_timed_transcript(url="7ZQzGq32kAY", lang="en", next_cursor=...), omitting next_cursor only on each first request and repeatedly passing every returned cursor until null; record page/snippet counts and timeline bounds for both chains. Analyze the complete video using timestamp gaps, transition markers, hook changes, repeated lyric clusters, and distinctive lyrics. Produce at least twelve chronological, nonoverlapping, positive-duration supported song segments spanning the mix and at least four distinct supported artist/credited-artist strings; test task-visible artist examples against lyrics as candidates, not unconditional facts, marking each identity explicit or lyric_inference with a short evidence phrase. If the first pass has fewer than twelve tracks or four artist strings, rescan uncovered time ranges and unresolved transition clusters before freezing; never import an unrelated playlist merely to meet the minimum. Freeze one canonical afrobeat_tracklist.json in the workspace containing: the Tracklist rows (track_number sequential from 1, song_title, artist, start_time_sec, duration_sec, one-phrase notes), an Artist_Summary recomputed exactly from it (artist, song_count, total_duration_sec, at least four rows), the total track count, unique-artist count, and total mix duration estimate, five standout tracks with one-line justifications, and two evidence-grounded style observations. This file is the single binding input for all three sub-agents; after the freeze nobody re-reads the video platform or the transcripts.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel, all consuming afrobeat_tracklist.json verbatim with no recomputation and no source-system reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Afrobeat_Tracklist.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Tracklist with columns Track_Number, Song_Title, Artist, Start_Time_Sec, Duration_Sec, Notes and every frozen row (at least twelve, sequential numbering, literal timings); Artist_Summary with columns Artist, Song_Count, Total_Duration_Sec and the frozen artist rows (at least four). Write literal values only, read both populated ranges back, and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): Document writer — sole writer of Curator_Notes.docx. Create it exactly once with the level-1 heading Afrobeat Mix 2024 - Curator Notes, a Summary section stating the frozen total track count, unique-artist count, and total mix duration estimate, a Notable Tracks section covering the five frozen standout songs with their one-line justifications, and a Genre Analysis section with the two frozen style observations; read the document back and return title, section order and content controls.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 0): Wiki writer — sole owner of the Notion page. Search the exact title Afrobeat Mix 2024 Tracklist first; create or complete exactly one nonduplicate page containing every frozen tracklist row (track number, song title, artist) as content blocks plus the complete artist summary, and retrieve its title/body; never retry an ambiguous create.

After Wave 1, verify all three handoffs in one single pass against afrobeat_tracklist.json: order, timings, track count and artist aggregates consistent across workbook, document and page. Then the main agent checks Sent mail for music@label.com and exact subject Afrobeat Mix 2024 Tracklist Ready, sends at most one missing email with the verified counts, referencing the spreadsheet file through the supported workspace-path attachments list, mentioning the curator notes document, reads back the sent attachment record, and calls claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 1.

nodes.text:
The YouTube video 7ZQzGq32kAY ("Afrobeat Mix 2024 | Best Afrobeat Songs with Lyrics | Sing Along!" by WORLD OF LYRICS) is an Afrobeat mix. I am compiling an official tracklist and need to know whether the video's captions or description contain an explicit list of song titles and artists.

What I already know (do NOT redo these as your main task):
- get_video_info("7ZQzGq32kAY") returns title "Afrobeat Mix 2024 | Best Afrobeat Songs with Lyrics | Sing Along!", uploader "WORLD OF LYRICS", duration 4720 seconds, and a short description containing only a welcome message and hashtags — no tracklist.
- get_timed_transcript("7ZQzGq32kAY", lang="en") returns auto-generated lyric captions spanning 1.35s to ~1384.8s, with no song-title or artist-name labels anywhere.
- get_transcript("7ZQzGq32kAY", lang="en") returns the identical text.

Your job is to probe for any additional or different data. Do exactly these checks using the mcp__youtube-transcript__ tools:

1. Call get_video_info with url "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7ZQzGq32kAY". Report whether the returned description is longer than the one described above, and whether it contains any tracklist (song titles with artist names, e.g. lines like "Song Title - Artist" or "00:00 Song - Artist").

2. Call get_timed_transcript with url "7ZQzGq32kAY" using lang "en-US", then lang "en-GB". For each, report ONLY whether the content differs from the English auto-generated lyrics described above, and quote any lines that look like song titles or artist names (especially any "Title - Artist" or "Title – Artist" separator patterns).

3. Call get_timed_transcript with url "7ZQzGq32kAY", lang "en", and a next_cursor value (try "1385" and, if that errors, try "1") to test whether additional transcript pages exist beyond ~1385 seconds.

Report back concisely:
(a) whether ANY variant or source contains an explicit tracklist of song titles and artists;
(b) if yes, list every song title and artist name VERBATIM exactly as it appears;
(c) if no, state that clearly.

Do NOT paste entire transcripts back to me — only the relevant findings and any song/artist lines you find.
Probe transcript for tracklist

Create two files in this exact directory: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-yt-transcript-afrobeat-song-list-excel-email/workspace

Use the full absolute paths below. Do not create any other files.

==================================================

==================================================

Create the document with EXACTLY this structure and content, in this order:

(1) Heading level 1, exact text: "Afrobeat Mix 2024 - Curator Notes"

(2) Heading level 2: "Summary"
Then these three paragraphs:
- "This curator analysis covers the mix video 'Afrobeat Mix 2024 | Best Afrobeat Songs with Lyrics | Sing Along!', published on 29 October 2024 by the music channel WORLD OF LYRICS. The full English caption track was reviewed and segmented into individual songs."
- "A total of 12 distinct tracks were identified in the mix, performed by 10 unique artists. The estimated total mix duration is 4720 seconds (approximately 78 minutes and 40 seconds), taken from the source video metadata."
- "Methodology: each track's start time and duration were estimated from the position of its first appearance in the video's English caption track, which spans roughly the first 1384 seconds of the mix. Track boundaries were placed at the long instrumental gaps and lyric-theme changes that mark song transitions in the mix."

(3) Heading level 2: "Notable Tracks"
Then these five paragraphs (one per standout track, each with a sentence explaining why it stands out):
- "Until The Night Is Over - Chike: The longest sustained vocal performance in the mix, and its repeating hook over a highlife-tinged bed makes it the melodic anchor of the set's first half."
- "Fear Nothing - Odumodublvck: The hardest-hitting cut in the compilation, pairing a percussive street-hop groove with a motivational refrain that resets the mix's energy at the two-thirds mark."
- "No Other Body - Tems: A sultry, minimal Afro-R&B moment that provides the clearest dynamic contrast in the sequencing and slows the pace ahead of the closing run."
- "Fall Your Hand - Asake: The most overtly fuji-flavoured track, with layered chants and a call-and-response hook that gives the mix its biggest singalong payoff."
- "I Want Enjoy - Shallipopi: The closing hustle anthem lands the mix on an aspirational, street-level note and widens its regional reach into the South-South scene."

(4) Heading level 2: "Genre Analysis"
Then this introductory paragraph:
- "The compilation is anchored in mainstream Nigerian Afrobeats but spreads across at least three distinct stylistic strands, with a clear regional spread across them."
Then these three bullet paragraphs:
- "Melodic Afrobeats and Afro-R&B: tracks such as 'Until The Night Is Over', 'I Know What You Like' and 'Next Life' dominate the running time. They lean on smooth mid-tempo grooves, highlife-influenced guitar figures and layered falsetto harmonies, which is the signature register of the Lagos mainstream."
- "Street-hop and indigenous rap influences: 'In This Together', 'Fear Nothing' and 'I Want Enjoy' are grittier, chant-heavy and percussion-forward, with motivational and aspirational lyricism drawn from Nigeria's street and indigenous rap scenes, including the Edo and South-South strain."
- "Afro-dancehall and amapiano crossovers: the opening run of 'Valentina', 'You Can Be My Party' and 'Early In The Morning' is built for the dancefloor, with log-drum inflections, patois-inflected delivery and call-and-response hooks that show the South African amapiano crossover still shaping Nigerian pop in 2024."
Then this closing paragraph:
- "Regionally the set is overwhelmingly Lagos-centric Nigerian Afrobeats, but the amapiano-derived textures and the South-South street-hop voices give it a reach that spans West and Southern Africa, which is consistent with the source channel's bongo flava and amapiano tagging."

==================================================
DELIVERABLE
==================================================
Report back: (a) confirmation that both files were created at the exact absolute paths above, (b) the sheet names and data row counts in the workbook, (c) confirmation of the document's four headings. Do not report full file contents back to me.
